mainTopic: ראשית הגז: why it is learned from מעשר בהמה, why it applies only to sheep, רבי יוסי's view on shearing and harvesting, and how many sheep obligate it
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining why רבי שמעון compares ראשית הגז to מעשר בהמה rather than בכור: an ordinary animal is best learned from an ordinary animal. It then looks for the source that ראשית הגז applies only to sheep. After a word-link of 'shearing' is challenged, the גמרא settles on רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching that the wool must be fit for the service of the כהנים. The word-link is then used to teach that sheep with hard wool are exempt. Two ברייתות disagree about wool that comes off when sheep are washed, and the גמרא explains them as רבנן versus רבי יוסי, who requires real shearing or harvesting. It then proves that רבי יוסי agrees when another method is the normal way, using לקט and onion beds. Finally, the גמרא discusses how many sheep obligate ראשית הגז: two, five, or four. רבי strongly backs רבי יוסי's four, and the גמרא challenges him with the rule that a third, in-between opinion does not decide.

steps.title: The list of shared laws with the firstborn ends, and it is longer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes listing the laws ראשית הגז shares with בכור, adding קדושה and מכירה, and points out that this list is longer than the one shared with מעשר בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ...in the matter of consecration, and sale. And these shared points are more numerous!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge against רבי שמעון. It adds the last two items to a list of ways ראשית הגז resembles בכור, then says: this list is bigger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון compares ראשית הגז to מעשר בהמה. The challenge is that ראשית הגז has more in common with בכור, including how consecration works and the כהן's ability to sell it. If we compare based on the most shared features, בכור should win.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecration, how and whether the item becomes holy
Sale, whether the item may be sold
Are more numerous
The first shearing of wool, given to a כהן
The animal tithe, every tenth animal

phrases.english: In consecration, and sale –
phrases.notes: These are the last two items in a list that started before this line, of laws ראשית הגז shares with בכור.

phrases.english: And these are more numerous!
phrases.notes: The shared points with בכור outnumber the shared points with מעשר בהמה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a challenge that began before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי שמעון's choice to learn ראשית הגז from מעשר בהמה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When choosing which case to compare to, pick the one with the most shared features. בכור has more in common with ראשית הגז.

steps.title: Ordinary is learned from ordinary
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון prefers to learn ראשית הגז, which applies to any animal, from מעשר בהמה, which also applies to any animal, not from בכור.
steps.simpleTranslation: He prefers to learn something ordinary from something ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. One shared feature, that both are 'ordinary' and not limited to firstborns, outweighs the longer list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראשית הגז and מעשר בהמה both apply to regular animals. בכור only applies to an animal that is born first. For רבי שמעון, this one basic similarity matters more than counting how many details match.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary, here: a regular animal, not a firstborn
It is preferable to him

steps.whatToRemember: Counting shared features is not the only way to choose a comparison. A single basic shared feature (both ordinary) can be stronger.
steps.confusionAlert: פָּשׁוּט here does not mean 'simple' or 'obvious.' It means an ordinary animal, as opposed to a firstborn.

phrases.english: Ordinary from ordinary is preferable to him.
phrases.notes: He means: ראשית הגז and מעשר בהמה both apply to any regular animal, while בכור only applies to a firstborn.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ranks one decisive similarity above a larger number of shared details.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Compare to whichever case shares the most laws, so learn from בכור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Compare ordinary to ordinary, so learn from מעשר בהמה.

steps.title: Where do we learn that first wool applies only to sheep?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule that ראשית הגז applies only to sheep and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first shearing applies only to sheep. From where are these words learned?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic by quoting the משנה. It asks what source tells us that ראשית הגז is only for sheep, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'your צאן,' and צאן can include goats too. So the גמרא needs a source that narrows it to sheep.

keyTerms.meaning: Does not apply
Ewes, sheep
From where are these words learned? A request for a source

phrases.english: The first shearing does not apply
except with sheep.
From where are these words learned?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that ראשית הגז is limited to sheep.

steps.title: Shearing here and shearing in איוב
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא learns from the word 'shearing': in איוב it is used with כבשים (sheep), so in ראשית הגז it also means sheep.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: It is learned from 'shearing' and 'shearing.' Here it is written, 'The first shearing of your flock you shall give him,' and there it is written, 'And he was warmed with the shearing of my sheep.' Just as there it is sheep, so too here it is sheep.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא answers by linking two פסוקים that both use the word 'shearing.' Since one clearly speaks about sheep, the other does too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ראשית הגז פסוק says צאן, which could include goats. The פסוק in איוב says כבשים, which means only sheep. By connecting the shared word, the narrow meaning moves over to ראשית הגז.

keyTerms.meaning: It comes, it is learned
Shearing
Flock, can include sheep and goats
Sheep, only sheep
Just as there, so too here, the comparison formula

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
It is learned from 'shearing' and 'shearing,'
phrases.notes: The same word shows up in two פסוקים, so we learn one from the other.

phrases.english: It is written here
"The first shearing of your flock you shall give him,"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4

phrases.english: and it is written there
"And he was warmed with the shearing of my sheep,"
phrases.notes: איוב 31:20

phrases.english: just as there it is sheep,
so too here it is sheep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A link through the word 'shearing' to the פסוק in איוב, which speaks only of sheep.

steps.title: Why not learn shearing from the firstborn instead?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: why not link 'shearing' to the בכור פסוק instead? It starts quoting a ברייתא about working and shearing a firstborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn 'shearing' from 'shearing' of the firstborn, as it is taught: 'You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox, and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock.' I only know an ox for work and a flock animal for shearing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב חסדא by offering a different word-link, to בכור. It begins quoting a ברייתא to show how shearing works with a בכור, setting up the point that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'shearing' also appears in the בכור פסוק. If the ban on shearing a בכור also covers an ox, then linking to בכור would make ראשית הגז apply to oxen too, not only sheep. The ברייתא starts with the plain reading and will go on to widen it.

keyTerms.meaning: And let us learn, a suggestion of a different source
Work, using the animal for labor
I only know, the plain reading before it gets widened

phrases.english: But let us learn 'shearing' from 'shearing' of the firstborn,
as it is taught:
"You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox,
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19

phrases.english: and you shall not shear the firstborn of your flock" –
I only know an ox regarding work
and a flock animal regarding shearing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב חסדא's choice of פסוק for the word-link.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's link of 'shearing' to the פסוק in איוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Shearing' also appears with בכור, where it may include oxen. Linking there would make ראשית הגז apply beyond sheep.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: work and shearing apply to both ox and sheep
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes. The ban on working applies to a firstborn sheep, and the ban on shearing applies to a firstborn ox, because the פסוק joins them with 'and'.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know to apply what was said about one animal to the other, and the reverse? The פסוק says: 'Do not work... and do not shear.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא it started in the last step. The ברייתא says the 'shearing' rule of בכור also covers oxen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Working is written about an ox, and shearing is written about a sheep. The ברייתא learns that each rule applies to both animals. So if 'shearing' in ראשית הגז is linked to the בכור פסוק, it would include oxen too, and not only sheep. That is the problem with רב חסדא's source.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not work (with a firstborn animal)
Do not shear (a firstborn animal)
Applying what was said about one case to the other
The פסוק teaches

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה,
phrases.english: From where do we know to apply what was said about this one to that one,
phrases.notes: 'This one' and 'that one' are the firstborn ox and the firstborn sheep.

phrases.english: and what was said about that one to this one?
The verse states: 'Do not work... and do not shear.'
phrases.notes: דברים 15:19. The word 'and' ties the two rules together, so both apply to both animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לִיתֵּן הָאָמוּר שֶׁל זֶה בָּזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in step 5. This completes the challenge to רב חסדא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's source that 'shearing' in ראשית הגז means sheep only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the בכור פסוק, 'shearing' covers oxen too. So linking ראשית הגז to that פסוק would include oxen, and the rule would not be limited to sheep.

steps.title: Oxen are left out: the wool must be fit for the כהן to wear
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק 'תתן לו' means the gift must be usable by the כהן himself, as clothing. Ox hair is only good for sackcloth, so oxen are not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'you shall give him', meaning for him to wear, and not for his sack.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why ראשית הגז still does not apply to oxen. The wool has to be good for the כהן's clothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if 'shearing' alone could include oxen, the words 'תתן לו' add a condition. The gift must be fit for the כהן to wear. Ox hair is only good for coarse sackcloth, so it does not qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall give him: the gift must be fit for the כהן himself
Sack or sackcloth: rough material, not clothing

phrases.english: The verse states: 'You shall give him,'
phrases.notes: דברים 18:4, the פסוק of ראשית הגז.

phrases.english: and not for his sack.
phrases.notes: He means: wool he can wear. Ox hair is only good for making sacks.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate word in the פסוק adds a condition that leaves out oxen
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the בכור 'shearing' includes oxen, ראשית הגז should too
steps.terutzMaskana: 'תתן לו' requires wool fit for clothing, and ox hair is not

steps.title: Then goats' hair should be included
steps.stepSummary: If the only test is 'fit for clothing', goats' hair can be worn. So ראשית הגז should apply to goats.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, goats' hair should be obligated!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. Goats' hair can be made into clothing, so why should it be left out?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 made 'fit for wearing' the deciding factor. Goats' hair passes that test, but the משנה says only sheep are included. So the answer from 'תתן לו' seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so: a challenge built on the last answer
Hair or down that is plucked
Goats

phrases.english: But if so,
goats' hair should be obligated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The 'fit for clothing' test from 'תתן לו'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Goats' hair is fit for clothing, so the test would include goats. That goes against the משנה's rule of sheep only.

steps.title: We need real shearing, and goats are not shorn
steps.stepSummary: ראשית הגז requires an act of shearing. Goats' hair is plucked, not shorn, so it is left out.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need shearing, and there is none!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the מצוה needs an actual shearing. Goats' hair is pulled out, not cut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two conditions: the wool must be fit for clothing, and it must come off by shearing. Oxen fail the first condition, and goats fail the second. Only sheep pass both.

keyTerms.meaning: We require
Shearing, or the shorn wool
There is not

phrases.english: We require shearing, and there is none!
phrases.notes: Goats' hair is plucked out, not cut with shears.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the goats' hair challenge from step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a second requirement: an actual act of shearing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Goats' hair can be worn, so it should be obligated
steps.terutzMaskana: Without shearing there is no obligation, and goats are plucked
steps.whatToRemember: Sheep are the only animal that passes both tests: wool fit to wear, and wool removed by shearing.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees when plucking is the normal way
steps.stepSummary: The idea that shearing is required comes from רבי יוסי. But he agrees that when an animal's hair is normally removed another way, the obligation still applies. So goats should be included.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who did you hear holds this idea? רבי יוסי. But רבי יוסי agrees in a case where that is its normal way!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the last answer. The opinion that requires shearing belongs to רבי יוסי, and he makes an exception when the usual method is not shearing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 depended on the rule that we need real shearing. The גמרא shows that the source of this rule, רבי יוסי, only requires shearing where shearing is normal. Goats are normally plucked, so by his own view their hair should be obligated, and the answer falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Line of reasoning or idea
Agrees or concedes
Something done in its normal way

phrases.aramaic: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא? רַבִּי יוֹסֵי –
phrases.english: Whom have you heard who holds this reasoning? Rabbi Yosei.

phrases.aramaic: הָא מוֹדֵי רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּמִידֵּי דְּאוֹרְחֵיהּ!
phrases.english: But Rabbi Yosei concedes in a case where that is its normal way!
phrases.notes: For goats, plucking is the normal way, so by this exception their hair would still count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer in step 9 by going back to the source of that rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that goats are left out because they are not shorn
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The only sage who requires shearing, רבי יוסי, makes an exception when the normal method is different. Goats are normally plucked, so that answer does not leave them out.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the discussion. The next step answers this challenge with a new source. Later, steps 19–21 show where we learn that רבי יוסי agrees when another method is the normal way.

steps.title: A new source: the gift must be fit for Temple service
steps.stepSummary: Since the shearing reason fell apart, the גמרא uses רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching. 'לעמוד לשרת' means the gift must be something fit for the service, which is sheep's wool.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is like רבי יהושע בן לוי said: 'to stand to serve' means something fit for the service. Here too, ראשית הגז must be something fit for the service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops its last answer and gives a new reason why goats and oxen are left out of ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 showed that 'it needs shearing' cannot keep goats out. So the גמרא changes the test: ראשית הגז must be fit for the service of the כהנים, and the בגדי כהונה are made from sheep's wool. Goats' hair and ox hair do not pass this test.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To stand to serve', a פסוק about the כהנים right after the מצוה of ראשית הגז
Something fit for the service in the מקדש
Here too, the same rule applies

steps.whyThisMatters: This becomes the main reason in the sugya why ראשית הגז applies only to sheep.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: Rather, it is as רבי יהושע בן לוי said:
"To stand to serve"
phrases.notes: דברים 18:5

phrases.english: means something fit for the service.
Here too, it must be something fit for the service.
phrases.notes: He means the wool must be the kind used for the clothing of the כהנים.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, כִּדְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the shearing reason, which step 10 knocked down, with a new source
steps.terutzResolutionType: New source replaces the rejected reason
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Goats are left out because their hair is not shorn
steps.terutzMaskana: Only something fit for the service, meaning sheep's wool, is included
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראשית הגז applies only to material fit for the service in the מקדש

steps.title: What is the word-link 'גיזה גיזה' for now?
steps.stepSummary: Now that 'לשרת' is the source, the גמרא asks what the גזירה שוה of 'גיזה' and 'גיזה' still teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does the link between 'shearing' and 'shearing' come to teach?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a follow-up question: if 'לשרת' already teaches the rule, what job is left for the word-link 'גיזה גיזה'? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not waste words or links. Once the main rule has a new source, the old גזירה שוה looks extra, so the גמרא has to find a new purpose for it.

keyTerms.meaning: The word 'shearing' appearing in two places, which links them through a גזירה שוה
What does it come to teach?

phrases.english: But then, 'shearing' and 'shearing':
what does it come for?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the new source in step 11, which seems to make the word-link unnecessary
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The purpose of the גזירה שוה once 'לשרת' is the source

steps.title: The word-link exempts sheep with hard wool
steps.stepSummary: The word-link is needed for the teaching of the school of רבי ישמעאל: sheep with hard wool are exempt from ראשית הגז, since the wool must be able to keep a person warm.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught: sheep whose wool is hard are exempt from ראשית הגז, as it says 'and he was warmed with the shearing of my sheep'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'גיזה גיזה' teaches a new detail: sheep with hard wool do not have to give ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in איוב connects 'shearing' with being warmed. Through the word-link, ראשית הגז covers only wool that can give warmth, so hard wool is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: Their wool is hard, rough wool that does not keep a person warm
He will be warmed

steps.whatToRemember: ראשית הגז applies only to sheep, learned from 'לשרת', and only to sheep with soft, warming wool, learned from the word-link 'גיזה גיזה'.

phrases.english: For what the school of רבי ישמעאל taught,
as the school of רבי ישמעאל taught:
Sheep whose wool is hard
are exempt from ראשית הגז,
as it says: "And he was warmed with the shearing of my sheep."
phrases.notes: איוב 31:20. Hard wool doesn't warm anyone, so it doesn't count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word-link teaches that sheep with hard wool are exempt, because the wool must be able to warm a person

steps.title: Two ברייתות disagree about wool from washing sheep
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא exempts both shearing goats and washing sheep. Another exempts shearing goats but obligates wool that comes off when sheep are washed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One ברייתא teaches: one who shears goats or washes sheep is exempt. Another ברייתא teaches: one who shears goats is exempt, but one who washes sheep is obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic by pointing out a contradiction between two ברייתות about wool that comes off sheep while they are washed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree that goats are exempt. They disagree only about sheep's wool that was washed off rather than shorn: is it included in ראשית הגז or not?

keyTerms.meaning: One ברייתא teaches this, and another ברייתא teaches that; a formula for showing a contradiction
Washing the ewes, which makes some wool come off
Exempt / obligated

phrases.english: One ברייתא teaches:
One who shears goats
or washes sheep is exempt,
And another ברייתא teaches:
One who shears goats is exempt,
but one who washes sheep is obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about wool that was not shorn
steps.kashyaTarget: The two ברייתות about washed-off wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They give opposite rulings on the same case: washed-off sheep's wool

steps.title: The two ברייתות follow רבנן and רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: There is no problem: the ברייתא that obligates follows רבנן, and the one that exempts follows רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult: this one follows רבנן, and that one follows רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying each ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that obligates washed-off wool follows רבנן. The ברייתא that exempts it follows רבי יוסי, who requires the normal act, here shearing. The next step shows where this argument comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; there is no contradiction
This one... and that one; matching each source to a different opinion

steps.confusionAlert: The order 'הא רבנן, והא רבי יוסי' does not follow the order of the ברייתות. The one that obligates is רבנן, and the one that exempts is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one follows רבנן,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא that says washing sheep makes you obligated.

phrases.english: and that one follows רבי יוסי.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא: הָא רַבָּנַן, וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction in step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source follows a different תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two ברייתות truly contradict each other
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן obligate washed-off wool and רבי יוסי exempts it

steps.title: The source: their argument about לקט
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about לקט is brought as the source of the argument. Its first, unnamed line excludes gleanings from picking by hand. רבי יוסי says only gleanings that come from actual harvesting count.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'the gleaning of your harvest', and not gleaning from picking. רבי יוסי says: לקט is only what falls because of harvesting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא where רבנן and רבי יוסי argue, to show where their views on washed-off wool come from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first line learns from 'your harvest' that gleanings from picking by hand are excluded. רבי יוסי says the מצוה applies only when the normal act, harvesting, is done. The same idea carries over to wool: for רבי יוסי only real shearing counts, so wool that comes off in washing is exempt, while רבנן obligate it.

keyTerms.meaning: Gleanings, stalks that fall during harvest and are left for the poor
Your harvest
Picking by hand instead of harvesting
Because of harvesting

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבי יוסי's view that the מצוה needs the normal act, the same idea mentioned in step 10, applies both to לקט and to ראשית הגז.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"The gleaning of your harvest"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:22

phrases.english: and not gleaning from picking.
רבי יוסי says:
There is no לקט
except what comes because of harvesting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the argument named in step 15
steps.raayaObject: That רבנן and רבי יוסי argue about whether only the normal act creates the obligation

steps.title: Isn't רבי יוסי Saying the Same Thing as the First Opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that in the ברייתא about לקט, רבי יוסי's view looks the same as the תנא קמא's.
steps.simpleTranslation: Wait, isn't רבי יוסי saying exactly what the first תנא said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks back at the ברייתא from step 16 and spots a problem. The two opinions do not look different at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said hand-picked gleanings are excluded. רבי יוסי said only gleanings that come from harvesting count, which also seems to exclude hand-picking. If they say the same thing, there is no real argument, and the proof brought in step 16 falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: The first opinion quoted in a ברייתא or משנה, with no name attached
That is the same as

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei is the same as the first tanna?
phrases.notes: Both opinions in the ברייתא from step 16 seem to exclude gleanings that were picked by hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how step 16 read the ברייתא as an argument between רבנן and רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 16 that the ברייתא records a real argument between רבנן and רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both opinions exclude hand-picked gleanings, there are not two views, so the ברייתא cannot show an argument.

steps.title: The Whole ברייתא Is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the entire ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, and the line with his name is just the reason for the first line.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole ברייתא is רבי יוסי's view. Read it like this: hand-picked gleanings are excluded, because רבי יוסי says that לקט is only what comes from harvesting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the problem by rereading the ברייתא. The first line is not a separate opinion. The second line explains it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there are no two opinions inside this ברייתא. Its first line simply follows רבי יוסי. The argument with רבנן still stands: רבי יוסי reads 'harvest' narrowly, just as he reads 'shearing' narrowly to exclude wool from washing, and רבנן do not read it that way.

keyTerms.meaning: The whole teaching follows one person's view
And this is what it means to say (a rereading of the text)
Gleanings: stalks that fall during harvest and must be left for the poor
Harvesting, cutting the crop

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the argument between רבנן and רבי יוסי is gone. It is still there. This ברייתא just records only רבי יוסי's side.

phrases.english: The whole of it is Rabbi Yosei,
and this is what it is teaching:
for Rabbi Yosei says,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לֶקֶט אֶלָּא הַבָּא מֵחֲמַת קָצִיר.
phrases.english: gleanings are only those that come because of harvesting.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּהּ רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הִיא, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 17 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: the whole ברייתא is one view, and the second line is the reason for the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא has two opinions, the תנא קמא and רבי יוסי, and they say the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is all רבי יוסי. 'Harvest' excludes hand-picking because only real harvesting counts.

steps.title: רבי יוסי Agrees When Hand-Picking Is the Normal Way
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרבא tells רב אשי that רבי יוסי agrees that לקט applies to a crop that is normally gathered by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרבא said to רב אשי: רבי יוסי agrees when hand-picking is the normal way to gather that crop.
steps.whatsHappening: A limit is put on רבי יוסי's rule. The proof for this limit comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי excludes hand-picking only when the crop is normally harvested with a tool. If a crop is normally uprooted or picked, then uprooting or picking is its 'harvest', and the מצוה applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, admits (in a certain case)
Something where this is its normal way

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that רבי יוסי's rule is about the normal way of gathering each crop, not about whether a tool was used.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרָבָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rav Acha son of Rava said to Rav Ashi:
Rabbi Yosei agrees regarding something whose normal way it is,
phrases.notes: He means a crop that is normally gathered by uprooting or by hand-picking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows רבי יוסי's rule from step 18. This is also the source for the claim made in step 10, that רבי יוסי agrees where another method is the normal way.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Even רבי יוסי applies לקט to hand-picked crops when hand-picking is the normal way to gather them.

steps.title: Proof from the Extra Words of the Verses
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יוסי: 'harvest' covers cutting, 'by reaping' adds uprooting, and 'when you reap' adds hand-picking.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יוסי says, from 'harvest' I only know about cutting. How do I know about uprooting? The פסוק says 'by reaping'. How do I know about picking by hand? The פסוק says 'when you reap'.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the proof for רב אחא's claim. רבי יוסי himself learns from extra words in the פסוקים that uprooting and hand-picking can also count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוסי always excluded hand-picking, he would not add it from a פסוק. So he must exclude it only when it is not the normal way. When it is the normal way for that crop, it counts as harvesting.

keyTerms.meaning: One who uproots the plant
One who picks or plucks by hand
The פסוק teaches (introduces the source)
From where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 18. In step 18 he excludes hand-picking from a crop that is normally cut. Here he includes it for a crop that is normally picked by hand.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei says:
"Harvest": I have only harvesting,
from where do we know one who uproots?
The verse says "by reaping,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:9

phrases.english: from where do we know one who picks by hand?
The verse says "when you reap."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:22

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings the source for the claim of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי applies לקט to crops normally gathered by uprooting or hand-picking.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא in which רבי יוסי learns uprooting and hand-picking from the extra words 'לקצור' and 'בקוצרך'.

steps.title: More Support: פאה from Onion Beds
steps.stepSummary: רבינא adds proof from a משנה: רבי יוסי requires פאה from each onion bed, even though onions are picked by hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: We also learned this in a משנה. Beds of onions among the vegetables: רבי יוסי says you leave פאה from each and every bed. The חכמים say you leave it from one bed for all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a second proof for the same idea. This time it comes from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Onions are pulled up by hand, not cut with a tool. Still, רבי יוסי requires פאה from them, and even from each bed separately. So he must agree that hand-gathering counts when it is the normal way for that crop.

keyTerms.meaning: We too have learned this (in a משנה), bringing support
Garden beds
The corner of the field left for the poor
From one on behalf of all

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי's rule that only 'harvesting' counts depends on the normal way of gathering each crop. For a crop normally picked by hand, like onions, hand-picking counts.

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
We too have also learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in פאה 3:4.

phrases.english: Beds of onions that are among the vegetables,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר: פֵּאָה מִכׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says: pe'ah from each and every one,
and the Sages say: from one for all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof, from a משנה, for the claim of step 19.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוסי applies the gifts for the poor to crops that are normally hand-gathered.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה פאה 3:4: רבי יוסי requires פאה from each onion bed, even though onions are gathered by hand.

steps.title: Why do בית הלל require five sheep?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's question about how many sheep count as 'many'. It understands בית שמאי, but asks for בית הלל's reasoning.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asks: how many sheep count as 'many'? בית שמאי's view makes sense, because even two sheep are called 'צאן'. But what is בית הלל's reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's question about the number of sheep. Then it challenges בית הלל: if two sheep are already called 'צאן', why do they need five?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי learn from a verse where two sheep are called 'צאן', so the מצוה fits two. בית הלל bring a verse about five sheep, but that does not show that two are not called 'צאן'. So the גמרא wants to know why בית הלל need the larger number.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Many': the amount of sheep needed to become obligated in ראשית הגז
'It makes sense for…': introduces one view that works before asking about the other
Sheep or flock. The verse uses this word for the מצוה of ראשית הגז
'What is the reason?'

phrases.english: And how many is "many"?
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה. There, בית שמאי say two sheep and בית הלל say five.

phrases.english: It makes sense according to בית שמאי:
two are also called "צאן".
phrases.notes: From their verse, ישעיהו 7:21: "and two sheep [צאן]".

phrases.english: But according to בית הלל, what is the reason?
phrases.notes: Their verse is שמואל א 25:18: "five sheep [צאן] made [עשויות]".

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of לקט and רבי יוסי to the next line of the משנה about ראשית הגז.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's requirement of five sheep
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Scripture calls two sheep 'צאן', so why should the מצוה need five?

steps.title: רב כהנא: 'עשויות' means two מצוות
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא explains that the plural word 'עשויות' shows that five sheep fulfill two מצוות‎: ראשית הגז and מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: the verse says 'עשויות' (made). This means the sheep are used for two מצוות‎: ראשית הגז and the gifts to the כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers for בית הלל by reading extra meaning into the word 'עשויות' in their verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse describes five sheep as 'made', in the plural. רב כהנא reads this as 'two מצוות are done with them'. So five sheep are the amount where ראשית הגז is added on top of מתנות, which shows that ראשית הגז needs five.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Made' (plural), from the verse about five sheep
The gifts given to a כהן from an animal that is slaughtered

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said:
The verse says "made",
phrases.notes: שמואל א 25:18, the verse בית הלל rely on.

phrases.english: meaning that they do two מצוות:
the first shearing and the gifts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about בית הלל's reasoning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading extra meaning into a word of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Two sheep should be enough, since they are called 'צאן'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'עשויות' shows that ראשית הגז only applies once there are five.

steps.title: Maybe the two מצוות are בכורה and מתנות?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two מצוות can't be בכורה and מתנות instead of ראשית הגז and מתנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why not say the two מצוות are the firstborn animal and the gifts?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא: his choice of ראשית הגז as one of the two מצוות seems random.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse only says 'two מצוות', a different pair could fit, like בכורה and מתנות. Then the verse would teach nothing about ראשית הגז, and בית הלל would have no proof.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Say instead…': suggests another way to read the source
The מצוה of a firstborn animal, which goes to the כהן

phrases.english: Say instead: the firstborn and the gifts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's choice of which two מצוות the verse means.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's reading of 'two מצוות' as ראשית הגז and מתנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another pair of מצוות could just as well be meant, so the verse does not prove anything about ראשית הגז.

steps.title: בכורה applies even to one animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that בכורה can't be meant, because even a single animal brings that obligation.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a firstborn, isn't even one animal obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא: בכורה can't be the second מצוה, because it does not need five sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse links the two מצוות to five sheep. בכורה already applies with just one animal, so it makes no sense to tie it to five. So the extra מצוה must be one that needs many sheep, which is ראשית הגז.

keyTerms.meaning: One (a single animal)
'Isn't it…?': a question that expects the answer yes
Is obligated (brings on the מצוה)

phrases.english: The firstborn: isn't one animal obligated?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that the pair is בכורה and מתנות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the other suggestion does not fit the number five
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two מצוות could be בכורה and מתנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: בכורה applies to one animal, so it can't be what the five sheep add.

steps.title: But מתנות also apply to one animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns the same logic around: מתנות also apply to a single animal, so רב כהנא's own pair has the same problem.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your own logic: with the gifts, isn't even one animal obligated?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the answer just given knocks out רב כהנא's own reading too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a מצוה that applies to one animal can't be one of the 'two מצוות', then מתנות can't be one of them either. So reading 'עשויות' as 'two מצוות' no longer works, and a new explanation is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And according to your reasoning…': turns the other side's logic back against them

steps.confusionAlert: This question does not bring back בכורה. It shows that the whole 'two מצוות' reading of רב כהנא falls apart, which is why רב אשי gives a new explanation.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
the gifts: isn't one animal obligated?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, מַתָּנוֹת, חֲדָא מִי לָא מִיחַיְּיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the logic of the previous answer against רב כהנא's own reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's reading that the two מצוות are ראשית הגז and מתנות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מתנות also apply to one animal, so by the same logic they can't be tied to five sheep.

steps.title: רב אשי: five sheep push the owner to do a מצוה
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reads 'עשויות' to mean that five sheep 'make' their owner do a מצוה, as if telling him to get up and do it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: 'עשויות' means that the sheep make their owners act. It is as if they say to him: 'Get up and do a מצוה!'
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב כהנא's reading fell apart, רב אשי gives a new explanation of the word 'עשויות' to support בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי does not count מצוות. He reads 'עשויות' as 'causing action': once there are five sheep, the owner becomes obligated in ראשית הגז. With fewer than five, the obligation of ראשית הגז has not started yet.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather': drops the earlier answer and brings a new one
Make someone act, push them to do
Their owner

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל need five sheep for ראשית הגז, because the verse calls five sheep 'עשויות', meaning they 'make' their owner do the מצוה‎ (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
"Made" means that they make their owners act,
phrases.notes: It's a play on the word: עשויות (made) is read like מעשות (make someone do).

phrases.english: and they say to him: "Get up, do a מצוה."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב כהנא's reading, which fell apart in the previous step.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reading of the word in the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'עשויות' means two מצוות are done, which proved unworkable.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'עשויות' means five sheep bring the owner into the obligation of ראשית הגז.

steps.title: A third view: four sheep
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי, in his father רבי יוסי's name, says four sheep are enough, based on a verse in שמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in the school of רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוסי, who said in his father's name: four, as it says, 'and four sheep [צאן] for the sheep'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a third opinion: ראשית הגז starts at four sheep.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the others, this view looks for a verse where a number of sheep is called 'צאן'. In the law of a thief who pays back, the תורה calls four sheep 'צאן', so four is the amount that brings the obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Of the school of': a teaching from a sage's study house
Four sheep: the number in this view
'In place of the sheep': a thief's payment for a stolen sheep

steps.whatToRemember: Three views on the amount for ראשית הגז: בית שמאי say two, בית הלל say five, and רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי in his father's name says four.

phrases.aramaic: תַּנְיָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
who says in the name of his father:
Four, as it is said:
"and four sheep [צאן] for the sheep."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:37

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם אָבִיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After explaining בית הלל, brings another opinion on the number of sheep.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ראשית הגז applies once a person owns four sheep, since a verse calls four sheep 'צאן'.

steps.title: רבי strongly backs רבי יוסי's opinion of four sheep
steps.stepSummary: רבי says we follow רבי יוסי (called בריבי) over בית שמאי and בית הלל, especially since רבי יוסי learns from the תורה and they learn from נביאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches: רבי said, even if their words came from the תורה and the words of בריבי came from נביאים, we would still listen to בריבי. All the more so now that their words come from נביאים and his words come from the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי's strong support for רבי יוסי's view that four sheep obligate ראשית הגז.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי and בית הלל learn their numbers, two and five, from פסוקים in נביאים, which are called דברי קבלה. רבי יוסי learns four from a פסוק in the תורה (step 28). רבי argues with a כל שכן: he would follow רבי יוסי even if the sources were reversed, so certainly now, when רבי יוסי's source is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The distinguished one', a title of honor; here it means רבי יוסי
Words learned from the five books of the תורה
Words learned from נביאים and כתובים
Had it been / even if
All the more so; an argument from the weaker case to the stronger one

steps.confusionAlert: Here קבלה does not mean 'oral tradition' in general. It means the books of נביאים and כתובים, as opposed to the five books of the תורה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step. Since רבי seems to decide the הלכה like רבי יוסי, the גמרא will ask how a middle opinion can be decisive.

phrases.english: It is taught: Rabbi said:
phrases.notes: This is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.english: Even if their words were words of Torah,
phrases.notes: 'Their' means בית שמאי and בית הלל.

phrases.english: and the words of the Distinguished One were from tradition,
phrases.notes: בריבי here is רבי יוסי. 'Tradition' means a source in נביאים or כתובים.

phrases.english: we would listen to the words of the Distinguished One,
and all the more so now that their words are from tradition,
and the words of the Distinguished One are words of Torah.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי: אִלְמָלֵא דִּבְרֵיהֶן דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds רבי's strong support to the opinion of רבי יוסי quoted in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We follow רבי יוסי's view of four sheep, all the more so because his source is in the תורה while the others' sources are in נביאים.

steps.title: A third, in-between opinion does not decide
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי: there is a rule that a third opinion between two others does not decide, so how can רבי יוסי's four win?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't the Master say: a third deciding opinion does not decide!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי's support for רבי יוסי by quoting a known rule about middle opinions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's four sits between בית שמאי's two and בית הלל's five. The rule says a third opinion like this is not decisive when it rests on its own reasoning. רבי יוסי uses a different פסוק from both of them, so following him seems to break that rule.

keyTerms.meaning: A third opinion that comes between two disputing opinions
Decides; settles the הלכה

phrases.english: But didn't the Master say:
A third deciding opinion does not decide!
phrases.notes: רבי יוסי's four falls between two and five, but he gets there from a different פסוק than either side.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר מָר: אֵין הַכְרָעָה שְׁלִישִׁית מַכְרַעַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי's claim in step 29 that we follow רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי's ruling that we listen to רבי יוסי's opinion of four sheep.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A middle opinion that is based on its own reasoning, not on the reasons of either side, cannot settle a dispute. רבי יוסי's four is just such a middle opinion.
